title: Tryton's workflow transitions write to mutable models, leaving no attributed record of the transition itself
content:
Tryton has workflows, and its transitions write to mutable models. The state a record is in is therefore recoverable at any moment, but the transition — the event of moving from one state to another, by whom, from what — is not retained as a first-class fact.

The distinction between a current state and a history of transitions is the whole argument for this cohort. Powerhouse holds the transition as an attributed, append-only business event. The workflow definition, the state machine and the business logic all stay in Tryton; only the historical record of what the state machine did moves.

Three small German Tryton partners carry this finding, one at "2 · next" and two at "3 · later". The paired demo scopes the work to a single Tryton module precisely so that partners of this size can deliver it themselves.
